summary: Audited 4 tier-2 pages (01, 21, 26, 14) — 01 is CLUSTER-READ-ELEC canonical and deserves the status with clear ownership split vs breakdown page; 21, 26, 14 are all thin procedural pages with 1-source CFPB/ConEd dependency, 94.7% br on 26 is a content-depth crisis, not a design issue.
findings: PAGE: 01-how-to-read-your-electric-bill — RATING: A — Well-structured, well-sourced, recently updated, clear process-first approach. Justified CLUSTER-READ-ELEC canonical.

PAGE: 21-past-due-balance-utility-bill-explained — RATING: D — Thin procedural page (58 lines), single CFPB source, no utility-specific detail, 88.9% br/32s TOP suggests users find nothing actionable.

PAGE: 26-utility-deposit-explained — RATING: D — 58 lines, one CFPB source, 94.7% bounce rate is a content-depth crisis. The page tells users to 'ask the provider' rather than providing any actual deposit rules, amounts, or state-specific guidance.
PAGE: 14-estimated-utility-bill-explained — RATING: C — Adequate but thin. Only ConEd sources, 76.5% br/19s TOP. Lacks the universal 'estimated bill' mechanics that users searching this slug expect.

01 vs breakdown-page overlap: 01 covers HOW to read (process, locate items, meter info, effective rate, TOU check). Breakdown page covers WHAT each charge means (supply, delivery, fixed, taxes, TOU mechanics). The ownership split is clean and defensible — 01 links to breakdown page twice. Both have distinct intents.
No remaining energy.gov/energysaver URLs found in the 4 audited pages. The 01 page uses energy.gov/save/home-upgrades references correctly via other pages, not in its own content.
All 4 audited pages are zero-outbound-source for utility-specific rules — they cite only EIA/CPUC/ConEd/CFPB, never state PUCs, actual tariffs, or deposit statutes. This is the site-wide E-E-A-T gap.

26-utility-deposit has 94.7% br on 81s TOP — users land, read the thin 'ask your provider' advice, and leave. The page must be expanded to include actual deposit rules (max 2× avg monthly bill for CA electric/gas per CPUC, state-by-state variations, credit-check alternatives, refund timelines).
